title: pixelNeRF: Neural Radiance Fields from One or Few Images
layout_note: Left half is a 3-D scene drawing (input view, encoder slab, feature grid, scene cube, target camera); a long curved arrow lifts one sampled point out to the right half, which is a flat row: (x, d) -> MLP f -> (RGB sigma) -> density plot -> loss below the plot.
grouping: No containers. Parts are named by plain serif labels under or above them (Input View, CNN Encoder, Target View, Volume Rendering, Rendering Loss). Colour ties the halves: the feature cell picked from W is a light-blue cuboid that reappears as the small cuboid beside W(pi x) under the MLP; purple and red underlines under x and d match the purple sample dots and red ray.
shapes_depth: Input view is a tilted image plane in front of a yellow slab (encoder) and a gridded black-outlined feature volume W; a light-blue cuboid is pulled from W toward the scene. The scene is a dotted wireframe cube holding translucent toy primitives (sphere, cube, plane), with a red ray carrying purple sample dots ending at a small camera glyph labelled d. The MLP f is four tall green-outlined unfilled rectangles. The volume rendering plot has a purple-to-cyan gradient density curve; the loss is a blue square minus g.t. inside norm bars.
proposed_highlight: The new conditioning is shown by geometry: a blue arrow projects the query point back onto the image feature grid, and the retrieved feature is drawn as a small blue cuboid feeding the MLP from below, the only side-input in the row.
lesson: Show image-conditioned rendering by projecting the query point on the ray back onto a gridded feature volume and carrying the picked cell, as a matching-coloured cuboid, into the MLP as a side input.
notes: venue from the arXiv comment CVPR 2021 (venue_source: arxiv-journal-ref); year 2021 is the venue year. Scene content is drawn toy geometry; parts of it (translucent primitives) are embedded as raster images, hence the measured photo_share.

measured.source: computed: paperfig kb measure (non-white pixels of a <= 800 px thumbnail, white = min(R,G,B) >= 245, minus the embedded images recorded by `refs crop` (images_px; their share is photo_share, null without a record); chromatic (RGB spread > 20) and neutral pixels clustered separately by PIL median-cut + k-means (k=8 / 3); clusters within dE00 4 merged; kept if >= 0.02 of chromatic pixels / neutral ones if >= 0.03 of all non-white pixels; share = fraction of the non-photo non-white pixels)

taxonomy.task: novel view synthesis from one or few images

core.what: a query point on a target-view ray in a 3-D scene is projected into the CNN feature volume W of the input view, and that fetched feature W(pi x) conditions the NeRF MLP f, drawn left to right from scene to rendering loss

relations.form: left cluster: input view card, yellow CNN encoder slab, gridded feature volume W and a wireframe cube with a red target ray and purple sample dots; a blue line projects one sample back onto a highlighted cell of W
the tuple (x, d) enters the green four-bar MLP f from the left and the fetched feature W(pi x), a small blue cuboid, enters it from below
left to right: scene, curved arrow from a sample point to (x, d), f, (RGB sigma), curved arrow into the volume rendering plot, curved arrow down to the rendering loss
the rendering loss draws the rendered blue pixel swatch against 'g.t.' inside a squared norm

channels.colour: colour ties symbols to geometry: purple underline on x = sample points, red underline on d = ray, blue underline on W(pi x) = the projected feature and its highlighted cell; green = the MLP, yellow = CNN encoder; the rendering curve uses a purple-to-blue gradient
channels.shape: cards = views, gridded slab = feature volume, bars = MLP, cuboid = a fetched feature, curve plot = density along the ray
channels.line: red = the camera ray, blue = projection to the feature grid, black curved arrows = stage hand-offs

quality.strengths: The method's addition to NeRF, fetching an image feature by projecting the query point, is drawn on the scene itself and made the largest element; colour underlines bind each symbol to the geometry it came from; the representations (x, d), W(pi x), RGB sigma and the rendered pixel are all drawn between the steps that make and consume them.
quality.weaknesses: The curved arrow from the sample point to (x, d), the arc from (RGB sigma) into the plot and the hook down to the loss all leave the straight reading line; the input view, encoder slab and feature grid overlap in one perspective stack, so where encoding ends and the feature volume begins is hard to see; the CNN encoder is labelled only below the stack.

insights.structure: Single left-to-right strip: a 3-D scene cluster on the left (input view, yellow CNN encoder slab, gridded feature volume W, wireframe cube with a red ray and target camera), then the MLP f as four green bars, then a volume-rendering plot and a rendering-loss equation stacked on the right.
insights.data: The input view and target view are flat schematic cards of colored shapes, the feature volume is a gridded 3-D slab, query samples are purple dots on the red ray, and the fetched feature W(pi x) is a small blue cuboid icon under f.
insights.emphasis: Color-coding ties symbols together: the purple underline on x and red underline on d match the sample dots and ray, and the blue underline on W(pi x) matches the projected feature patch.
insights.flow: A curved black arrow lifts the ray sample out of the 3-D scene into (x,d), then straight arrows run right through f to (RGB sigma), a curve drops into the density plot, and a final curve drops to the loss below.
insights.avoid: The left 3-D cluster overlaps encoder, feature grid and scene cube so tightly that the projection pi x is hard to see; the projection of x onto W is implied, not drawn.

arrangement.units: no enclosures; three loose clusters (3-D scene with encoder, MLP with its inputs, rendering plot with loss) separated by whitespace
arrangement.inputs_as: schematic image card of colored shapes plus a target camera glyph
arrangement.losses_at: right, under the volume-rendering plot as a norm equation
